page.layout: One printed page, single column of text, with a title block at the top and a large woodcut initial beginning the first paragraph. Faint show-through from the reverse page is visible in the right half and is not transcribed. Signature mark "ij" at the foot right.

main_text.head: ILLVSTRISSIMO ET POTENTISSIMO PRINCIPI ac domino D. Gulielmo Principi Auraico Comiti Nassæuo &c. Christi gloria assertori in Hollandia & Zelandia fortissimo, Gratiam & pacem à Domino.
main_text.p: VEtus est illud, Princeps Illustrisime, etiam ab Aristotele vsurpatum, Nihil esse in ipsa rerum vniuersitate pulchrius ordine. Quid enim vel oculis iucūdū, vel menti etiam ipsi & animo hominis gratum obuersari potest, quod sit confusum, & nulla partium apta seperatione distinctum? Certè quocunque nō tantum oculos, sed omnes animi sensus cōuerterimus, si quæ in eos incurrunt, neque ordine digesta, neque apto situ inter se cohærētia, neque conuenienti loco & modo collocata à nobis apparebūt: ea neque vtilitatem, neque venustatem aliquam habere statim pronuntiabimus, tantúmque ab illis oculorum, animíque intuitum auer-ij.

page.notes: The initial V is a large decorated woodcut letter, transcribed as V. Lines "Etus est" and "Vetus" read as printed: the initial is the first letter, rendered VEtus. The page-end mark "¶ ij." is the gathering signature. Some words near the initial and in the right margin are show-through from the reverse and were omitted. Spelling such as "Illustrisime", "seperatione", "Nassæuo" follows the print as best read; "Illustrisime" and "seperatione" may be printing errors. Line-end "auer-" is continued on the next page.
